As shown in Figure ES-4, the domestic value for systems installed during 2024 primarily comes from domestic racking, trackers, and CdTe modules as well as inverters to a much smaller degree. Per the domestic content bonus credit criteria, domestic CdTe modules already qualify as having a domestic cell, and the Series 7 module produced by First Solar contains 100% domestic components as defined by the IRS table, which means it also qualifies for the domestic production value in the table. While the domestic content average in this diagram is well below the minimum investment tax credit threshold of 40% for 2024, it represents an average of many systems, which can vary significantly in content. We estimate that up to 8 GW of systems met the domestic content dc bonus criteria in 2024. Based on domestic production in 2024—documented throughout this report—we expect the installed capacity in 2025 that meets the domestic content bonus criteria to greatly increase. 5 This analysis assumes a 1-year delay between shipping and installation; therefore, the Sankey diagrams reflect 2024 PV installation totals but rely on 2023 manufacturing totals and sourcing. The data in this section rely heavily on utility system installation totals, and technical features reported by the U.S. Energy Information Administration are presented in the Discussion section. Total 2024 installation data are from the International Energy Agency’s Photovoltaic Power Systems Programme data provided by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Solar Energy Technologies Office.
